notes: CONTROL CASE HELD UP LIVE: this was one of the five hand-resolved naming collisions, specifically checked to declare `destination_folder_id` flat at the top level of the body with no json_path and no wrapper object. Built exactly that way on attempt 1 and it worked — a real positive result, not a hollow PASS (the response is the full v2 test_case object, not just {status,body}). Final folder for TC-54458 (int 1975349) is 764828 (the disposable child of __scratch__/764138), confirmed via list_folder_test_cases on BOTH folders (764138 dropped from count 2 to 1, losing 1975349; 764828 rose from count 0 to 1, gaining it) and via get_test_case (folder_id 764138 -> 764828). This is a genuine move, not a 200-that-didn't-move-anything. Every declared field in the nested 200 schema was checked against the actual response: nothing declared was missing (folder_path, feature/background/scenario, reviewers/review_status were all absent, but the contract itself documents each of those as conditional/write-response-absent, so their absence here is expected, not drift) and nothing undeclared appeared beyond the nested schema. HOWEVER: the FLAT `returns` array (used for the top-line contract summary) omits `is_shared` and `attachments`, both of which are declared in the nested 200 schema AND both of which were actually returned — a flat/nested disagreement, consistent with the standing finding that the flat returns array is unreliable; not counted as declared_missing/undeclared_returned since the nested schema (the trustworthy one) already covers both fields. Only three things changed on the case as a result of the move: folder_id (764138->764828), urls.self (folder segment updated to embed the new folder id, confirming the numeric id is recoverable only by parsing this URL), and last_updated_at (bumped to the write timestamp). identifier, title, steps, tags, owner, custom_fields, created_at, created_by and updated_by were all byte-for-byte unchanged, matching the contract's explicit guidance that 'nothing but the folder changes'. No folder-count fields (cases_count/sub_folders_count) are exposed by this capability at all — it returns a test_case object, not a folder object, so that data point from the folder-mutation siblings does not apply here. No 500s, no environment flakiness (status 0) encountered on any of the 7 calls made (1 move + 6 setup/verification reads) — preprod was responsive throughout. TC-54458 is left resident in folder 764828 for the sibling update_test_case probe to find.
